content.overview: BNS s. 271 — Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life. BNS restatement of IPC 269. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 269. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 271 is the rule on “Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life”. The section provides that . Whoever unlawfully or negligently does any act which is, and which he knows or has reason to believe to be, likely to spread the infection of any disease dangerous to life, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 271 exists so that “Negligent act likely to spread infection of disease dangerous to life” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.
